How to become a doctor in the US

Follow the US path from college science prerequisites and the MCAT to medical school, residency and state licensure. See how it differs from studying in Poland.

What subjects do you need?

The matura gives you a foundation for college courses. The MCAT also covers biochemistry, physics, psychology, sociology and critical reading. You might read about an enzyme experiment and predict the result if one condition changes. School-level protein structure is a starting point for that reasoning.

AAMC’s MCAT outline
Admission
You usually start with four years of college. You choose a major, complete the courses required by medical schools, and typically take the MCAT admissions exam. Pre-med describes this preparation for applying to medical school.
Medical school
Medical school usually takes four years. Basic sciences and clinical rotations lead to an MD or DO degree. Both are physician qualifications.
Licence to practise
A state medical board issues the licence. It checks the degree, licensing exams (USMLE or COMLEX-USA), and required postgraduate training. Eligibility for an unrestricted licence varies by state.
Specialty training
Residency is paid, supervised work and training in a specialty. It typically takes at least three years. A fellowship provides further training in a narrower field.

Harvard Pathways · United States

After college, MD students study foundations and integrated human pathophysiology alongside the longitudinal Practice of Medicine course. The main clinical clerkships (Principal Clinical Experience) begin in MD year 2. When comparing that with UZ year 2, count the time since secondary school as well.

Harvard · Pathways curriculum map

Polish medical degree, US residency

If you earn your medical degree in Poland and want to enter US residency, you apply as an international medical graduate (IMG). Start by checking your school and graduation year under Sponsor Notes in the World Directory of Medical Schools. On the standard route, ECFMG verifies your education and requires USMLE Step 1, Step 2 CK, and evidence that you meet clinical and communication requirements. Applying for a residency position is a separate step.
